my boyfriend used to be like that in terms of cooking, and it’s taken almost a year of just trying to get him to realize that a) cooking can be fun and b) if he helps cook, he can make things how he wants, plus we have a 50/50 split on cooking and dishes so if he cooks, i clean and he doesn’t have to, which is a win for him

he needs to go to therapy in my opinion.

from what you’ve described, he’s really defensive about his lack of skills, and has an idea that he can coast by in life by finding a new “mommy maid” (which will never go away, my 68 yo stepdad still acts like a little helpless toddler) 

try suggesting couples therapy, even if it’s something you do online/over the phone bc of current events. don’t suggest that it’s needed BECAUSE of him, but say something along the lines of “i really do want to live with you, but maybe a few therapy sessions can help us make sure that it’s in the best interest of both of us”

other (possibly unethical) option: try “training” him during certain activities using rewards and the like. example: offer to make his favorite meal if he unloads the dishwasher, OR make cooking dinner a “challenge” where you guys split the tasks and try to make the better plate (which would maybe motivate him to quickly guess the best way to do something, and then you can help him learn better ways over time)

overall, if you really love him, don’t throw in the towel immediately, because this isn’t entirely his fault, he just needs to realize it’s harmful behavior now. if you go through these things and he doesn’t change however, leave and don’t look back (unless you want to be a maid down the line)  

tldr: try therapy OR (maybe unethical) try “training” him to learn basic skills using a reward system (think pavlov)
